akh.text: Djeru was a faithful initiate and leader of the Tah crop on Amonkhet, and as a child he showed his friends Samut and Nakht a hole in the Hekma, which led them into the desert, where Nakht withered to a husk and Djeru tackled Samut out of sight.
The loss hardened his faith while Samut took up doubt, and as an initiate he faced the trials, in one of which he drowned Meris in a serpent pool and cut out his heart to pay Bontu's toll.
Samut begged him not to enter the final Trial, but he refused, and in the battle that followed he surrendered his khopesh and prayed for her glorified death.

When Hazoret struck, Samut tackled him out of the way and Gideon blocked the spear, which left Djeru enraged that his chance at a glorious death was gone; later, as the Gate opened on endless wastes, he publicly declared he stood with Samut against the God-Pharaoh.

hou.text: Djeru loses faith in the God-Pharaoh, declaring that Samut was right and that he lied.
Samut urges him to lead people out of the city, and the two reunite and rally surviving initiates against the Scorpion God and the Eternals.
The living bring down the Scorpion God by driving it onto an obelisk, and Hazoret vows to stand by the mortals.
